research.summary: Macro backdrop is mildly supportive: the Fed cut rates 25bp on 2025-12-10 (target 3.50-3.75%) and SPY sits ~1% below its high, but commentary warns January volatility could pick up after a calm 2025 close. Momentum leaders GE (+84% in 2025, at 52-week high), GOOGL (+28% 90d), and CAT (+58% in 2025, record $39.9B backlog, AI power theme) dominate the reference allocation, with GE and LLY technically overbought (RSI 74.7/77.4). Company news is net constructive for GE, XOM, JPM, and NVDA, mixed for CAT (expected Q4 earnings pullback) and GOOGL (valuation criticism), and cautious for MSFT (AI-competition doubts).

opportunities: GE has the strongest 12-minus-1-month momentum (+72.9%) with +11.0% 30d outperformance vs SPY and a fresh 52-week high — the reference allocation's top pick is technically confirmed, though RSI 74.7 and 30.3% vol warrant position-size discipline.
GOOGL combines +65.7% 12-1 momentum and +28.4% 90d with a constructive flat 30d consolidation just -2.5% off its high — trend intact without overbought RSI (54).
CAT offers top-three momentum (+62.9% 12-1, +22.3% 90d) with RSI reset to 40.1 during the 30d pause — better entry risk than GE/LLY among the momentum leaders.
GLD (+60.9% 12-1, +12.3% 90d at 17.5% vol) and JNJ (+47.7% 12-1 at 16.5% vol) provide the best momentum-per-unit-volatility and diversify the industrial/tech concentration of the reference book.
XOM at a 52-week high (+6.3% 30d) and JPM (+5.7% 30d, -1.1% from high) confirm broadening cyclical leadership; PLD is a low-vol (13.0%) near-high momentum alternative.
risks: Momentum leaders are expensive short-term: GE RSI 74.7, LLY RSI 77.4, and LIN RSI 83.1 (a counter-trend bounce below its SMA-200) are all prone to mean reversion on a 5-day horizon.

The reference 3x33% GE/GOOGL/CAT book is highly concentrated in names running 30%+ annualized vol — a single-name shock moves the whole portfolio; max_position_weight 0.35 does not cap this concentration.
Mega-cap tech is fracturing: MSFT is below its SMA-200, META below all SMAs (-17.6% off high), AAPL oversold (RSI 31) — index-level strength masks narrow, rotating leadership.
SPY momentum is weak (+0.5% 30d, RSI 46) and defensives/consumer (PG, HD, SO, AMT, SHW) are in downtrends, so any benchmark pullback would likely hit high-beta momentum names hardest.
TLT's flat, low-vol range gives no rates hedge signal, leaving the book without a clear defensive ballast if the equity consolidation resolves lower.

forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call as of 2026-01-02 for the 5-trading-day horizon (next decision 2026-01-09), using only price history through the decision date. Method is a drift-based statistical model: expected return is an estimated drift over the horizon, with p10/p90 from the return distribution implied by recent (30d) annualized volatility, roughly lognormal. Benchmark comparison: SPY expected +0.32% over the same horizon, so only GE (+1.37%), GOOGL (+1.01%), CAT (+0.99%), GLD (+0.99%), JNJ (+0.75%), NVDA (+0.74%), JPM (+0.71%), and LLY (+0.68%) show positive expected excess return; most names are statistically indistinguishable from the benchmark at this horizon. Confidence reflects the probability that the point-estimate direction is correct given interval width (z = |mu|/sigma, sigma = (p90-p10)/2.645); all values are near 0.5-0.64 because 5-day drift signals are weak relative to volatility. Limitations: drift estimates over 5 days are extremely noisy and dominated by volatility; intervals are wide (e.g., NVDA p10 -7.84% to p90 +10.12%) and represent uncertainty, not a recommendation to avoid; the model uses no news, fundamentals, or cross-asset correlation structure; fat tails and regime shifts are not captured; RSI extremes (LLY 77.4, LIN 83.1, GE 74.7) and momentum signals are not incorporated beyond the drift term.

decision.rationale: The critic verified the momentum core is real (GE +72.9%, GOOGL +65.7%, CAT +62.9% 12-1), so I keep all three but size GE down from the reference 33% to 20% given RSI 74.7, 52-week-high crowding and 30% vol, and redeploy into GLD (forecaster's highest-confidence call at 0.64, +60.9% 12-1 at 17.5% vol) plus JNJ and PLD, the two best momentum-per-volatility diversifiers the analyst flagged and the forecaster's screen wrongly excluded. CAT is retained at 19% because its RSI-40 reset offers the best entry among the leaders and its Q4 earnings almost certainly print after the Jan-9 window, while GOOGL's intact trend (RSI 54, -2.5% off high) justifies the largest weight. The book's gross expected ~0.99% less ~10bps of entry costs yields ~0.9% net vs SPY's +0.32%, with portfolio vol reduced from the reference's three correlated 30%-vol names to roughly 14-15% annualized.

forecaster.method_notes: Statistical drift-based forecast over the 5-trading-day horizon (2026-01-09 to 2026-01-16) using only price history through the decision date; p10/p90 intervals derived from recent realized volatility (30d annualized) scaled to the horizon. forecaster.method_notes: Drift-based statistical forecast over the 4-trading-day horizon (2026-01-16 to 2026-01-23) using only data through the decision date; p10/p90 are 80% intervals. Benchmark SPY is expected +0.26% over the horizon, so expected returns must be judged against that, not zero: largest positive excess vs benchmark are GE +0.74, CAT +0.66, GOOGL +0.59, GLD +0.59, JNJ +0.43; PG is the only negative-excess name (-0.43). Confidence is the implied probability the direction call is correct, derived from expected return scaled by interval width; over 4 days expected drift is small relative to uncertainty (p10-p90 spans ~4-16 pct pts), so most directional calls sit near 50-60% and should be treated as weak signals. Limitations: the drift model ignores news, RSI extremes and mean reversion (e.g., AAPL RSI 10.6, HD/SHW/CAT RSI ~74-79), volatility clustering, and cross-asset correlation; wide intervals reflect genuine 4-day uncertainty, not a reason to avoid an asset; expected returns for most tickers are statistically indistinguishable from the SPY benchmark at this horizon.

forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call as of 2026-01-23 for the 5-trading-day horizon (next decision 2026-01-30); no data after the decision date used. Method is drift-based: expected return from recent drift estimates, with p10/p90 intervals scaled from 30-day annualized vol to the 5-day horizon; direction assigned by the tool (up/flat/down vs zero). Benchmark comparison: SPY expected +0.35% over the horizon, so only GLD (+1.19%), CAT (+1.16%), GOOGL (+1.05%), GE (+1.05%), JNJ (+0.91%), NVDA (+0.63%), LLY (+0.57%), XOM (+0.53%) and NEE (+0.50%) clear the benchmark on expected return; all other names are within noise of SPY. Confidence is a signal-to-noise heuristic (0.5 + 0.5*|expected|/interval width, capped 0.9) and is uniformly low (~0.50-0.66) because 5-day expected drifts are tiny relative to interval widths - wide intervals here reflect genuine uncertainty, not avoidance signals. Limitations: drift over 5 days is statistically weak and dominated by idiosyncratic/event risk (e.g., in-window earnings for several names, GLD's RSI 88 overbought state, AAPL RSI 12.4 oversold rebound potential); the model ignores news, earnings dates, vol clustering, and fat tails, so realized tails can exceed the p10/p90 band; intervals are symmetric around the drift and do not condition on the current portfolio or momentum signals beyond the drift term.

forecaster.method_notes: Statistical drift-based forecast over the 5-trading-day horizon (2026-01-30 to 2026-02-06) using only data through the decision date; one universe-wide call covering all 25 tradable tickers plus the SPY benchmark. Expected returns are small relative to 5-day dispersion (p10-p90 spans roughly 4-17 percentage points), so directional confidence is modest everywhere; confidence scores scale with expected return relative to interval width. All returns should be judged against SPY's expected +0.31%: the clearest positive excess-return signals are GLD (+0.81pp), GOOGL and CAT (+0.76pp each), GE (+0.71pp), JNJ (+0.59pp), LLY (+0.40pp), and NVDA (+0.33pp); HD, PG, AMT, MSFT, SHW, V, LIN, CVX, SO, TLT, and AMZN show negative expected excess returns. Wide intervals reflect genuine short-horizon uncertainty, not a reason to avoid an asset. Limitations: symmetric percentile bands understate tail risk and ignore fat tails, jumps, and event/news catalysts (e.g., earnings) within the window; drift estimates over 5 days are weakly identified and mean-reversion or momentum continuation at daily frequency is not explicitly modeled; vol estimates use 30-day annualized figures that may not reflect regime shifts; no fundamental or news information is incorporated.

I again reject the reference's 33% GE leg (30d -1.6% and 90d -2.27% both lag SPY, below SMA-20, stale 12-1 momentum) and its 33% GOOGL sizing ahead of next week's earnings print, redeploying part of the proceeds into NVDA (recovering uptrend above rising SMAs, +0.33pp expected excess) and LIN (lowest-vol diversifier with consistent 30d/90d outperformance). The ~21% cash weight is a deliberate buffer against the GOOGL/LLY earnings gaps and post-nomination macro volatility, with total turnover costs (~3bps) immaterial.

Rotation into 'real' assets is pronounced: energy (XOM +25.8%/30d), staples (WMT, PG, JNJ at all-time highs), utilities (NEE) and gold are beating the market, while MSFT (-17%/30d) and AMZN (-13%/30d after its $200B 2026 capex plan spooked investors Feb 5) bear the brunt of AI cash-flow concerns. forecaster.method_notes: Drift-based statistical forecast over the 5-trading-day horizon (2026-02-06 to 2026-02-13) using only price history through the decision date; one forecast_universe call covered all 25 tradable tickers plus the SPY benchmark. Expected returns are small relative to the 10th-90th percentile interval widths, so signals should be judged against the SPY benchmark forecast (+0.30% expected, p10 -3.09%, p90 +3.80%) rather than zero: CAT (+1.21%), GLD (+1.14%), GOOGL (+1.02%), GE (+0.98%), JNJ (+0.93%) and NVDA (+0.87%) show the largest positive excess returns, while MSFT, AMZN, HD, AMZN-like laggards and AMT sit modestly below benchmark. Confidence is scaled from the expected return relative to interval width and is uniformly low (0.50-0.53), reflecting weak short-horizon signal strength. Limitations: the drift model ignores news, earnings, mean reversion and regime shifts; several names carry extreme RSI readings (JNJ 95.1, XOM 84.2, PG 83.7, CVX 78.1, WMT 76.9) that raise pullback risk not reflected in the central estimate; high-volatility names (LLY, GLD, META, NVDA) have very wide intervals, so their p10-p90 ranges represent uncertainty rather than conviction; and 5-day expected returns are near noise level, so the forecast is best used for relative ranking, not point prediction.

decision.rationale: I keep the multi-horizon momentum core (GOOGL 18.9%, CAT 8.7%, WMT, JNJ, XOM, GLD, NVDA, NEE) but reject the reference's 3x33% concentration because CAT is parabolic after a verified +7.1% Feb 6 spike (53% above SMA200) and GOOGL is the book's main exposure to the still-unresolved AI-capex repricing cycle; instead I resolve the critic's flagged GE gap by adding 9% GE (3rd-best 12-1 momentum at +59.1%, RSI 48.8, consolidating above a rising SMA stack) plus 5% JPM (clean uptrend, RSI 58, financials led the Feb 6 rally), while exiting dead-weight LLY (49.7% vol for +0.24% excess) and LIN (no trend, negative excess) and trimming the RSI-extended cluster (JNJ 95, WMT 77, XOM 84) per the critic's mean-reversion warning about the drift model's optimistic bands. GLD stays at reduced 6.2% size given its 47% vol and crash history despite the #2 forecast rank, and ~20% cash is retained as an observed-risk buffer against a renewed AI-panic leg and the overbought leadership cluster. Turnover is ~14% one-way (~3bp cost, immaterial) and the changes are substantive repositions, not cosmetic; I expect a modest positive week driven by the energy/industrial/staples rotation with SPY itself offering no beta tailwind.

forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call as of 2026-02-20 for the 5-trading-day horizon (next decision 2026-02-27). Method: drift-based statistical model using only price history through the decision date; p10/p90 intervals scale 30-day annualized volatility to the 5-day horizon. Benchmark SPY is forecast at +0.29% (p10 -3.1%, p90 +3.79%), so expected returns should be judged against that, not zero. Relative to SPY, the strongest 5-day expected excess returns are CAT (+1.17%), GLD (+0.82%), GOOGL (+0.75%), GE (+0.72%), JNJ (+0.66%), XOM (+0.38%), NEE (+0.35%), NVDA (+0.45%); MSFT, META, AMZN, V, HD, PG, AMT, SHW, TLT and LIN are forecast at or below benchmark. All expected returns are small relative to interval widths (roughly +/-3% to +/-7% at the 10th/90th percentiles), so directional calls are weak and confidence values are modest (0.50-0.58), scaled by expected return relative to interval width. Limitations: drift estimates over 5 days are dominated by noise; the model ignores news, fundamentals, and regime shifts; Gaussian intervals understate fat tails and vol clustering; high-volatility names (LLY, META, GLD, NVDA, MSFT) have especially wide intervals, meaning wide intervals reflect uncertainty rather than a signal to avoid; overbought RSI readings (GE 80, JNJ 76, CAT 73, LIN 72) are not modeled and could cap upside.

I again reject the reference 3x33% CAT/GOOGL/GLD book: it stacks 37%/23%/48% vol names including one in an active breakdown, and the critic correctly shows GLD's forecast downside is understated ~2x versus its own 48% vol. The ~22% cash buffer is a deliberate hedge against the NVDA earnings gap, the Iran deadline and renewed tariff whiplash, costing only ~6bps of forgone SPY drift over 5 days.

forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call as of 2026-02-27 for the 5-trading-day horizon (next decision 2026-03-06); drift-based statistical model using only decision-date history: expected return from estimated drift, p10/p90 from 30d annualized vol scaled to 5 days (approx. normal/lognormal bands). Benchmark SPY expected +0.25% (p10 -3.14%, p90 +3.76%); all excess returns are measured against that, not zero. Only GOOGL (+0.77pp), JNJ (+0.72pp), CAT (+1.22pp), GE (+0.72pp), GLD (+0.91pp), XOM (+0.48pp) and NEE (+0.44pp) show positive expected excess return; all are small relative to their 5-day bands, so direction calls are low-conviction (confidence = implied probability the sign matches, derived from expected return vs band width). Limitations: no news, earnings, or event adjustments (e.g., NVDA print read-throughs); vol estimated from a 30d window may under/overstate near-term dispersion; assumes roughly symmetric return distribution and ignores fat tails, gaps, and cross-asset correlation; 5-day drift estimates are statistically weak, so wide intervals reflect genuine uncertainty rather than avoidable risk.

forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call as of 2026-03-06 for the 5-trading-day horizon (next decision 2026-03-13); drift-based statistical model using only price history through the decision date. p10/p90 are 10th-90th percentile return bands from 30d annualized volatility scaled to the horizon; expected returns are small relative to band widths, so directional confidence is modest (confidence = 0.5 + |expected|/band width, capped). forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call as of 2026-03-13 for the 5-trading-day horizon (next decision 2026-03-20). Method is drift-based: expected return is a small momentum/drift estimate and the p10-p90 band scales each ticker's 30-day annualized vol to 5 days, so intervals are wide relative to means. Benchmark comparison: SPY expected +0.27% (p10 -3.1%, p90 +3.75%); only CAT (+1.46%), GOOGL (+1.16%), GLD (+1.06%), NVDA (+0.89%), XOM (+0.78%), GE (+0.78%), JNJ (+0.77%), CVX (+0.57%), NEE (+0.56%) and WMT (+0.52%) clear the benchmark on expected return, but with 5-day intervals of roughly +/-3-8% none of these edges is statistically decisive - wide intervals are uncertainty, not evidence against a position. Limitations: pure statistical/price-history method using only data through the decision date; no news, fundamentals, or regime shifts are incorporated; Gaussian bands understate fat tails and gap risk (notably for high-vol names LLY 49%, GLD 48%, NVDA 42%, CAT 41%); drift estimates over 5 days have very low signal-to-noise, so direction calls near zero (flat) should be treated as low-information; confidence scores are heuristic (expected return relative to band width), not calibrated probabilities.

AAPL.notes: Below SMA-20/50 and hovering at SMA-200 (247.55 vs 246.01) with RSI 23.9; 30d/90d both trail SPY. Oversold but no uptrend structure to lean on.

MSFT.notes: Deep downtrend: -19.6% over 90d, price 20% below SMA-200 and -29% off 52w high. 12-1 momentum (+3.5%) has fully decayed vs SPY's +22%.

NVDA.notes: Below all SMAs with 40% annualized vol; 12-1 momentum (+59.9%) masks a negative 30d. High-beta downside risk in a correcting tape.

GOOGL.notes: Best large-cap tech chart: flat 30d/90d, +85% 12-1 momentum, and price 16% above SMA-200, though below SMA-20/50. Consolidation within a dominant uptrend.

META.notes: Below all SMAs, -24.7% off 52w high, RSI 28.3. Negative on every horizon vs SPY.

AMZN.notes: Flat 30d but still below SMA-20/50/200 and -19% off the high; 90d -7.2% lags. Stabilizing, not turning up.

HD.notes: Worst 30d in the universe (-14.7%), RSI 14.1, below all SMAs. Capitulation-style decline with no support structure.

WMT.notes: Pullback within an uptrend: +46% 12-1 and +3.1% 90d beat SPY, price still 10.6% above SMA-200, but below SMA-20/50 after a -4.5% month.

PG.notes: Staples defense has broken down: -9% 30d, RSI 14.9, below SMA-200. Negative 12-1 momentum (-3.4%) confirms relative weakness.

JPM.notes: Below all SMAs with -8.6% 90d; 12-1 (+31.5%) still ahead of SPY but the short-term trend has rolled over.

V.notes: Persistent downtrend: -12.2% 90d, -18.7% off high, below all SMAs, negative 12-1 momentum. Underperforms on every horizon.

LLY.notes: -11.4% 30d and -12.8% 90d with 33% vol; only the SMA-200 (887) is holding. Momentum leadership has reversed hard.

JNJ.notes: Multi-horizon outperformer: +12.5% 90d and +54.9% 12-1 vs SPY, above SMA-50/200 with just 16% vol. The -4.2% month is a pullback to SMA-50, not a trend break.

XOM.notes: Strongest book holding: +5.8% 30d, +36.9% 90d, +35.3% 12-1 all beat SPY; at 52w high above rising SMAs, RSI 62 not stretched.

CVX.notes: Best 30d in the universe (+9.2%) with +36.2% 90d, at 52w high above all SMAs. RSI 72.4 is overbought — expect choppiness, but trend is intact.

CAT.notes: Sharp -10.5% month has broken below SMA-20/50 with 37.7% vol, but price remains 28% above SMA-200 and 12-1 momentum (+127.7%) is the universe's best. High-vol consolidation within a major uptrend.

GE.notes: -14.2% 30d on 34.9% vol has broken SMA-200 (286.43 vs 290.66); RSI 16.7. The 12-1 (+63.5%) signal is stale relative to current price action.

NEE.notes: Mild dip within an uptrend: +12.2% 90d and +33% 12-1 beat SPY, above SMA-50/200, only -5.8% off the high. Defensive growth holding up well.

SO.notes: Above SMA-50/200 with +8.2% 90d vs SPY -2.9%; shallow -1.8% 30d. Steady utility uptrend, though 12-1 (+9.6%) trails the benchmark.

LIN.notes: Flat 30d but +16% 90d crushes SPY's -2.9%; above SMA-50/200 with 19.6% vol. Recent-horizon outperformance is the strongest in the defensive complex.

SHW.notes: Worst 30d in universe (-14.9%), RSI 12.5, below all SMAs. No technical support until SMA-200 at 342.

PLD.notes: Range-bound: flat 90d, above SMA-200 but below SMA-20/50, RSI 19.3. Oversold but directionless.

AMT.notes: Below SMA-200 and -22.5% off the high with 31.8% vol and negative 12-1 momentum (-10.5%). Weakest REIT on structure.

TLT.notes: Low-vol (11.3%) drift around SMA-200; -3.9% 30d offers no hedge confirmation yet. Bonds are not yet paying off in this equity drawdown.

GLD.notes: Violent -10% month on 34.3% vol, RSI 14.8, but price is still 10.4% above SMA-200 and 12-1 momentum (+63.5%) is second only to CAT. Correction within a secular uptrend, not a breakdown.

SPY.notes: Benchmark in correction: below SMA-20/50 and now below SMA-200 (645.3 vs 653.2), RSI 25.9. Broad beta is a headwind for the entire equity book.

opportunities: XOM and CVX are the only names positive on both 30d and 90d horizons, at 52-week highs above rising SMAs with 12-1 momentum beating SPY — the clearest expected-outperformance candidates; CVX RSI 72 argues for trimming into strength rather than adding.

JNJ offers the best risk-adjusted profile: +12.5% 90d and +54.9% 12-1 vs SPY, above SMA-50/200, only 16% vol, and the 30d dip is an orderly pullback to SMA-50 — a candidate to hold or add on weakness.
LIN and NEE combine positive 90d momentum (+16.0% and +12.2% vs SPY -2.9%) with above-SMA-50/200 structure and below-average vol; both defend the book while SPY sits below its SMA-200.
GLD at RSI 14.8 after a -10% month, while still 10% above SMA-200 with +63.5% 12-1 momentum, is a tactical mean-reversion candidate — but only as a hold/oversold bounce, not a fresh momentum add.
GOOGL is the one mega-cap tech with intact structure (flat 30d/90d, +85% 12-1, 16% above SMA-200) and would be the first tech name to rehabilitate if the market stabilizes.
risks: SPY has broken below its SMA-200 with RSI 25.9 — a confirmed market correction means high-beta holdings (CAT 37.7% vol, GE 34.9%, GLD 34.3%) face amplified downside; the book's 10% cash buffer is thin.

Momentum decay is hitting the portfolio's biggest 12-1 winners: CAT -10.5% and GE -14.2% over 30d despite +128% and +63% 12-1 signals — the reference's 33% CAT/GOOGL/GLD momentum book is chasing stale signals into a drawdown.

GE has lost SMA-200 support and is the weakest current holding on trend, vol, and 30d momentum — prime trim candidate; SHW/HD/PG-style capitulation (RSI <15) shows the selloff is broad, not idiosyncratic.
Energy concentration: XOM + CVX = ~22.6% of the book with correlated crude exposure; a commodity reversal would hit both simultaneously, and CVX is already overbought (RSI 72).
TLT is not hedging: -3.9% 30d with price below SMA-200 means the bond allocation is failing exactly when diversification is needed; GLD's -10% month also questions the defensive pairing.
WMT has broken below SMA-20/50 after a -4.5% month — if the 90d outperformance (+3.1%) rolls over, the defensive consumer leg weakens alongside everything else.

forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call as of decision date 2026-03-20, horizon 5 trading days (next decision 2026-03-27). Method: drift-based statistical model — expected return from historical drift, p10/p90 from 30d annualized volatility scaled to 5 days (approx. normal quantiles). Benchmark SPY forecast: +0.31% (p10 -3.02%, p90 +3.75%); excess returns vs SPY are modest, with CAT (+1.04pp), GOOGL (+0.85pp), GLD (+0.54pp), GE (+0.48pp), XOM (+0.45pp) the only names meaningfully above benchmark. Confidence = implied P(return>0) from mu/sigma of the interval; all values sit near 0.5 because 5-day drift signals are weak relative to volatility. Limitations: drift over 5 days is dominated by noise; intervals assume near-normal returns and understate fat tails and gap risk; no news, fundamentals, or mean-reversion conditioning (several names are deeply oversold — HD RSI 14, SHW 12.5, PG 14.9, GLD 14.8 — so realized outcomes could deviate materially from drift in either direction); wide intervals reflect uncertainty, not a recommendation to avoid assets.

decision.rationale: I exit GE (lost SMA-200, RSI 16.7, -14.2% 30d) and GLD (broken 30d momentum, sovereign-seller tail risk, rate-hike repricing) and trim CAT/SO, converting the book's weakest and most rate-exposed sleeves into a 20.6% cash buffer against a confirmed SPY correction (below SMA-200, RSI 25.9) and the ceasefire binary on the 23.7% energy sleeve, while again rejecting the reference's 33% CAT/GOOGL/GLD momentum book. Proceeds tilt to XOM (only name positive on both 30d and 90d, at 52-week highs with RSI 62) and JNJ (best risk-adjusted trend at 16% vol, +12.5% 90d, fresh FDA catalyst), plus a measured 6% GOOGL — the sole mega-cap now beating SPY on every horizon (30d -0.5% vs -5.0%, 90d +1.5% vs -2.9%, 12-1 +85% vs +22%), which updates my prior rejection now that its trend has repaired. Per the critic I discount the drift model's CAT/GLD 'up' labels, hold CVX at 9.7% rather than adding at RSI 72, and expect this cash-cushioned, defensively tilted book to grind out roughly +0.4% against a flat-to-choppy benchmark.

forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call (drift-based statistical model) covering all 25 tradable tickers plus SPY benchmark over the 9-trading-day horizon (2026-03-27 to 2026-04-10), using only data through the decision date. Expected returns are modest relative to interval widths: the benchmark SPY is forecast at +0.44% (p10 -4.01%, p90 +5.10%), so names should be judged on excess return vs SPY, not vs zero. Strongest expected excess returns: CAT (+2.10%), GOOGL (+1.37%), XOM (+1.11%), JNJ (+1.02%), GLD (+0.98%); weakest: AMT (-1.11%), PG (-0.95%), META (-0.92%). Confidence is scaled from the ratio of expected return to interval width, so all values sit near 0.5-0.58, reflecting genuinely low signal-to-noise at a 9-day horizon. Limitations: drift models capture trend persistence but not mean-reversion at RSI extremes (XOM/CVX overbought at RSI 82-84; MSFT/META/LLY oversold at RSI 9-18), ignore news, earnings, and macro catalysts, and assume roughly lognormal returns; wide p10-p90 bands (roughly +/-5-10%) are uncertainty, not a recommendation to avoid any name. High-volatility names (NVDA, META, LLY, GLD, GE) carry the widest intervals.

forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call as of 2026-04-10 for the 5-trading-day horizon (next decision 2026-04-17); drift-based statistical model using only price history through the decision date. Benchmark SPY is expected +0.41% over the horizon, so only CAT (+1.73%), GOOGL (+1.41%), NVDA (+1.05%), GE (+0.85%), GLD (+0.84%), WMT (+0.79%) and JNJ (+0.78%) show positive expected excess returns; all other tickers are within noise of the benchmark. Key limitation: 5-day expected returns are an order of magnitude smaller than the 10-90 percentile interval widths (roughly +/-3% to +/-7%), so directional calls are low-conviction and intervals reflect uncertainty, not avoidance signals. The model assumes no regime change, ignores news, earnings, and macro events, and does not capture fat tails or momentum-crash dynamics flagged in the prior decision summary; RSI>70 names (AMZN, CAT, NEE, SO, SHW, JPM, PLD) carry elevated mean-reversion risk not reflected in the drift estimate.

forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call as of 2026-04-17 for the 5-trading-day horizon (next decision 2026-04-24). Method: drift-based statistical model using only price history through the decision date; expected returns are 5-day drift estimates and p10/p90 intervals are scaled from each ticker's 30-day annualized volatility (roughly +/-1.28 sigma over 5 days). Benchmark comparison: SPY drift is +0.68% over the horizon, so only CAT (+1.33pp), GOOGL (+0.99pp), NVDA (+0.80pp), GE (+0.50pp), and modestly JNJ/WMT/PLD/JPM/GLD show positive expected excess return; most defensives (PG, SO, LIN, AMT, TLT, V, HD, SHW) are expected to lag SPY. Limitations: (1) 5-day drift estimates are dominated by noise; expected returns are small relative to interval widths, so direction calls are low-conviction; (2) intervals assume roughly lognormal returns with constant vol and ignore vol clustering, fat tails, and gap risk; (3) the model uses no news, fundamentals, or post-decision-date data; (4) several tickers show extreme overbought RSI (SPY 96.7, AMZN 97.6, META 96.4, GOOGL 93.8, NVDA 92.5, MSFT 92.8) and XOM/CVX deeply oversold RSI (18.3/22.7), mean-reversion risk the drift model does not capture; (5) wide intervals (e.g., META -6.13% to +7.83%) reflect genuine uncertainty, not a signal to avoid. SPY is included in the tool output for benchmark comparison only and is excluded from the tradable forecast list.

forecaster.method_notes: Drift-based statistical forecast over the brief's 5-trading-day horizon (2026-04-24 to 2026-05-01), using only price history through the decision date; one forecast_universe call supplied all tickers including benchmark SPY (included here for comparison only, not tradable). Expected returns are small drift estimates relative to 5-day noise: SPY benchmark is +0.58% [-1.79, +3.01], so names should be judged vs that anchor, not zero. Largest positive excess vs SPY: CAT +1.48pp, GOOGL +0.95pp, NVDA +0.64pp, GE +0.30pp, JNJ +0.26pp; largest lags: AMT -0.86pp, PG -0.74pp, V -0.71pp, HD -0.63pp. Confidence per name is a normal-CDF mapping of |expected return| divided by the interval-implied 5-day sigma, so all values sit near 0.5-0.68: direction calls at this horizon are low-conviction and wide p10-p90 bands reflect genuine uncertainty, not avoidance signals. Limitations: price-only method ignores earnings, macro releases, and gap risk; assumes approximately lognormal returns scaled from 30d annualized vol with no fat tails; does not model mean-reversion risk after overbought conditions (AMZN RSI 95, SPY 88, NVDA 87, GOOGL 83, CAT 84) or oversold bounces (XOM 27, JNJ 30, SO 33), which could skew realized outcomes versus the symmetric intervals shown.

forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call as of 2026-05-01 for the 5-trading-day horizon (next decision 2026-05-08). Method is drift-based: expected return is a momentum/drift estimate from history through the decision date only; p10/p90 are 10th/90th percentile return bands from 30-day annualized vol scaled to 5 trading days, so intervals are wide relative to the small drift and direction calls are weak (e.g., GOOGL +1.88% expected but p10 -3.41%). All returns are compared to the SPY benchmark forecast (+0.68% expected, p10 -1.62%, p90 +3.02%), not zero: CAT (+1.56pp excess), GOOGL (+1.20pp), NVDA (+0.71pp) lead; AMT (-0.96pp), PG (-0.85pp), HD (-0.76pp) lag. Limitations: no mean-reversion adjustment for overbought RSI (GOOGL 86.8, AMZN 83.3, CAT 75.2, SPY 79.3) or oversold names (JNJ 34.6, HD 36.2), no earnings/news/event risk (GOOGL/AMZN earnings recently in window), vol estimated from a 30-day window may understate regime shifts, and 5-day drift signals have low signal-to-noise; confidence values reflect interval width and excess-vs-benchmark magnitude, capped near 0.6.

forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call (drift-based statistical model) for all 26 tickers over the brief's 5-trading-day horizon (2026-05-15 to 2026-05-22), using only data through the decision date. Expected returns are modest (roughly -0.5% to +2.0%) and should be judged against the SPY benchmark forecast of +0.55%, not zero: CAT (+1.99%), GOOGL (+1.72%), NVDA (+1.33%), XOM (+0.90%), AAPL (+0.81%), JNJ (+0.79%) and CVX (+0.75%) clear the benchmark; AMT (-0.45%), HD/SHW (-0.33%), PG (-0.17%), V (-0.11%), MSFT (-0.05%) and TLT (0.0%) lag it. Confidence is capped near 0.5-0.6 because 5-day p10-p90 intervals (roughly 3.6% for TLT to 13.9% for LLY, scaled from 30-day annualized vols) are several times wider than the point forecasts, so directional calls are weakly identified. Limitations: the drift model assumes persistence of recent trend and does not capture mean reversion, news, earnings, or regime shifts; several names show overbought/oversold RSI extremes (AAPL 88.5, GOOGL 76.9, LLY 75.2 vs META 26.7, HD 25.9, SHW 26.7) and parabolic 12-1 momentum (CAT +122.9%, GOOGL +103.9%) that raise pullback/catch-up tail risk not reflected in the symmetric intervals; vol estimates from the last 30 days may understate or overstate near-term dispersion; no fundamental or news information is incorporated.

forecaster.method_notes: Drift-based statistical forecast over the 4-trading-day horizon (2026-05-22 to 2026-05-29) using only data through the decision date; p10/p90 intervals scale 30-day annualized vol to the horizon. Benchmark SPY is forecast at +0.40% (p10 -1.53%, p90 +2.36%), so expected returns must be judged against that, not zero: only CAT (+1.48%), GOOGL (+1.38%), NVDA (+0.87%), JNJ (+0.69%), XOM (+0.61%), AAPL (+0.60%), CVX/LLY/GLD/GE (+0.51-0.55%) show positive excess return, and all are within one interval-width of the benchmark. At a 4-day horizon, expected returns are small relative to interval widths, so direction calls are weak and confidence is capped near 0.6; wide intervals (META, LLY, NVDA, CAT, GE) reflect high realized vol, not avoidance signals. Limitations: no news/event or earnings adjustment, assumes vol and drift persistence, does not model fat tails or regime shifts, and ignores mean-reversion risk from stretched RSI readings (AAPL 91.3, SPY 72.1, PLD 71.4, LIN 68.4) and oversold conditions (WMT/NEE RSI 32.1); SPY included as benchmark comparison only.

Forecast rankings are treated as noisy drift artifacts per the critic; this book targets a modest positive excess return (~+0.15% over SPY's +0.40%) with materially reduced tail risk, and I expect the window direction to be up.

forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call as of 2026-05-29 for the 5-trading-day horizon (next decision 2026-06-05). Method: drift-based statistical model using only price history through the decision date; expected returns are annualized drift scaled to 5 days, and p10/p90 bands are derived from 30-day annualized vol scaled to the horizon (sqrt-time). Benchmark SPY forecasts +0.49% (-1.66% to +2.69%); all comparisons should be made against that, not zero. At a 5-day horizon expected returns are small relative to interval widths, so most names are statistically indistinguishable from the benchmark: only GOOGL (+1.13pp excess), CAT (+1.30pp), and NVDA (+0.37pp) show positive excess drift, while HD, SHW, PG, V, AMT show the largest negative excess. Confidence scores are heuristic, inversely related to interval width and vol (TLT/SPY/JNJ/SO highest; META/LLY/CAT/GOOGL/NVDA lowest). Limitations: no news, fundamentals, or cross-asset correlation information is used; drift estimates are noisy at short horizons; sqrt-time scaling ignores vol clustering and fat tails, so realized 5-day moves can exceed the p10-p90 band; RSI extremes (AAPL 84.3, LLY 81.1, WMT 25.9) and mean-reversion effects are not modeled.

forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call as of 2026-06-05 for the 5-trading-day horizon (next decision 2026-06-12); drift-based statistical model using only price history through the decision date. Benchmark SPY expected +0.49% (p10 -1.69%, p90 +2.72%); all comparisons should be made against that, not zero. Highest expected excess returns vs SPY: CAT +1.42%, GOOGL +1.04%, LLY +0.42%, AAPL +0.40%, JNJ +0.39%, NVDA +0.38%; only CAT and GOOGL clear the benchmark by more than ~1pp with meaningful conviction. forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call as of 2026-06-12 for all 25 tradable tickers plus SPY benchmark over the 9-trading-day horizon (2026-06-12 to 2026-06-26). Method: drift-based statistical model — expected return from estimated drift, p10/p90 from volatility scaled to the horizon (approximately normal, p50 = expected). Confidence is the model-implied probability that the stated direction materializes, derived from expected return divided by the p10-p90-implied sigma. Benchmark comparison: SPY expected +0.82% (p10 -2.11%, p90 +3.85%); only CAT (+2.65pp), GOOGL (+1.85pp), JNJ (+0.80pp), LLY (+0.66pp), NVDA (+0.59pp), XOM (+0.53pp), AAPL (+0.48pp), CVX/PLD (+0.39pp), and GE (+0.26pp) show positive expected excess return vs SPY, and most of these sit within one sigma of the benchmark, so excess returns are not statistically decisive. Limitations: purely quantitative, price-history-only (no news, fundamentals, or event calendars); assumes stationary drift and roughly lognormal returns over 9 days, so it ignores earnings, macro shocks, and regime changes; at this short horizon drift signals are small relative to volatility (intervals of ±3-9% vs expected returns of ±0.3-3.5%), meaning direction calls are low-conviction and wide intervals reflect genuine uncertainty rather than avoidable risk; high-volatility names (CAT, NVDA, META, GE, LLY) have especially fat tails not fully captured by the normal approximation.

research.summary: The week ending 2026-06-26 was defined by an 'AI memory shock': Micron's blowout quarter confirmed AI-driven memory demand, but the resulting memory-price surge pressured AAPL, MSFT and AMZN, and the Nasdaq fell five straight days as investors rotated out of tech/AI into pharma, materials and blue-chip Dow names. Healthcare is the clear momentum leader — LLY hit an all-time high on EMA backing for Jaypirca and Medicare inclusion for its obesity drugs, JNJ hit new highs on positive IMAAVY data — while GE sits at 52-week highs with a $170B services backlog. Company-specific negatives: Alphabet's stock plunged after a second high-profile AI talent exit (John Jumper), Apple's Vision Pro hardware chief defected to OpenAI, and OpenAI is building a custom chip with Broadcom that threatens NVDA pricing power. Macro overlays are mixed: Trump accused Iran of violating a ceasefire, crude is cracking (XOM/CVX weak), Bitcoin is near a two-year low, and the Fed remains data-dependent.

forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call (one of 10 budgeted) covering all 25 tradable tickers plus SPY benchmark over the brief's 9-trading-day horizon (2026-06-26 to 2026-07-10), using only data through the decision date. Method is drift-based: expected return from recent drift, with p10/p90 percentile bands scaled from 30d annualized vol to the 9-day horizon. Benchmark comparison: SPY expected +0.75% (p10 -2.24%, p90 +3.83%); only CAT (+2.92pp), GOOGL (+1.57pp), JNJ (+1.03pp), GE (+0.82pp), LLY (+0.63pp), and AAPL (+0.55pp) show positive expected excess return, and most names' expected returns are small relative to their interval widths, so differences vs SPY are weakly identified. Wide intervals (e.g., NVDA, META, LLY, CAT at 15-22pp spans) reflect high 30d realized vol, not a reason to avoid; TLT's tight band reflects its low vol. Limitations: statistical drift model ignores news, fundamentals, mean reversion, and regime shifts; symmetric bands understate fat tails and gap risk; 9-day horizon is short enough that 12-1 momentum signals have limited predictive power; RSI extremes (HD, GE, JNJ, SHW overbought; GOOGL, XOM, CVX oversold) suggest possible short-term reversals not captured by the drift estimate; confidence scores are heuristic, scaled to expected-return magnitude relative to interval width.

decision.rationale: I reject the 33%-weight CAT/GOOGL/JNJ reference stack for an eighth week: CAT's 49% vol and Friday's Dow-dragging drop, GOOGL's AI talent-exodus headlines on a -13% 30d tape, and single-name concentration outweigh the forecaster's bullish calls, which the critic showed are method-inconsistent and news-blind. I trim the SMA-200-testing tech block (GOOGL 8.7->6.0, AMZN 7.6->5.5, NVDA 6.9->5.0) where the five-day Nasdaq slide, OpenAI/Broadcom chip threat, and AMZN's capex/regulatory overhang are live 9-day risks, and redeploy into the rotation leaders with multi-horizon momentum and fresh positive catalysts: JNJ to 11.5% (12-1 +56%, IMAAVY data, normal 24.5% vol), LLY to 9.5% (30d +11.6%/90d +34.9% at highs on EMA/Medicare wins), GE to 7.5% (best 30d +16.3%, $170B backlog), while holding JPM/CAT/PLD/TLT/LIN/AAPL unchanged and keeping 13.1% cash as justified ballast against the active tech rotation and geopolitical headline risk. Treating the forecast layer as one noisy input per the critic, I expect roughly +0.9% for the book vs SPY +0.75% over the window, with ~12% one-way turnover costing only ~1-2bps.

forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call (one-shot budget) covering all 25 tradable tickers plus SPY benchmark, horizon 5 trading days (2026-07-10 to 2026-07-17), using only data as of the decision date. Model is a drift-based statistical forecaster: expected return from recent drift/momentum, with an 80% interval (p10-p90) scaled by 30d annualized volatility; direction labeled from the sign/magnitude of expected return. Confidence is a heuristic 0.5 + 0.45 * |expected| / half-width of the interval, so it reflects signal strength relative to uncertainty, not probability of positive return. Key comparisons vs benchmark: SPY expected +0.42% over 5d; only CAT (+1.79%), GOOGL (+1.35%), JNJ (+1.06%), AAPL (+0.88%), LLY (+0.84%), GE (+0.68%), PLD (+0.62%), NVDA (+0.57%) show expected excess returns above ~+0.1pp, while MSFT (-0.89pp), AMT (-0.84pp), META (-0.59pp) lag. All expected returns are small relative to interval widths (e.g., CAT +1.79% vs -4.79%/+8.81%), so no single-name edge is statistically decisive at this horizon; wide intervals reflect high vol (META/CAT ~54% annualized), not a reason to avoid. Limitations: pure quantitative drift/vol model with no news, fundamentals, or cross-asset correlation; 5-day drift estimates are dominated by noise; intervals assume approximately lognormal returns with stable volatility and understate fat tails and gap risk; TLT/GLD vol regimes can shift with macro surprises not captured here.

decision.rationale: I reject the 33%-weight CAT/GOOGL/JNJ reference stack for a ninth week: CAT's +129.9% 12-1 is an outlier at 53.8% vol below its SMA20, GOOGL's edge is stale 12-1 momentum on a -1.9% 30d tape below SMA50, and JNJ carries RSI 73, a freshly affirmed $45M talc verdict, and a Q2 print inside the window. Instead I concentrate in the names with persistent multi-horizon relative strength and moderate vol — AAPL and GE (the only two beating SPY on 30d/90d/12-1, AAPL at 52-week highs) plus LLY (+24.7% 90d, analyst PT raises) — while trimming JNJ to 8.5% and JPM to 7.5% to shrink binary earnings exposure, cutting decaying-momentum PLD/GOOGL and high-vol CAT/AMZN. The 18% cash weight is deliberate insurance against the JPM/JNJ earnings binaries, SPY sitting -0.35% from highs, and US-Iran crude whipsaw; TLT stays at 5.5% only as cheap 9%-vol ballast, not a counted-on hedge, and total turnover (~17% one-way, ~2bps cost) is well justified by the risk reduction.

forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call (drift method) for all 26 tickers over the brief's 5-trading-day horizon (2026-07-17 to 2026-07-24), using only data through the decision date. Expected returns are small relative to the 80% intervals (p10-p90 roughly +/-2-7%), so no ticker's edge is statistically decisive at this horizon; confidence values are implied probabilities that the point-estimate direction is correct given each interval's width. Benchmark comparison: SPY expected +0.37% over 5 days; only CAT (+1.23pp), GOOGL (+0.94pp), JNJ (+0.63pp), AAPL (+0.54pp), LLY (+0.46pp), and PLD (+0.36pp) show positive excess vs benchmark, while MSFT (-0.81pp) and AMT (-0.79pp) lag. Limitations: drift-based estimates ignore mean reversion, volatility clustering, fat tails, and event/news risk; extreme RSI readings (AAPL 88.7, XOM/CVX ~73, TLT 19.7) and stretched 12-1 momentum (CAT +131%) are not modeled and could drive sharp reversals; 5-day horizons are dominated by noise, so wide intervals reflect genuine uncertainty rather than a signal to avoid assets; no fundamentals or news were incorporated.

forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call as of 2026-07-24 for the 5-trading-day horizon (next decision 2026-07-31). Method is drift-based: expected return is a statistical drift estimate from price history through the decision date only; p10/p90 are 10th/90th percentile return intervals scaled by each ticker's recent annualized volatility (30d). All expected returns are small relative to interval widths, so confidence is modest (0.50-0.58), scaled by |expected|/(p90-p10). Benchmark comparison: SPY drift is +0.35% (p10 -1.90%, p90 +2.65%); only CAT (+1.20pp), GOOGL (+0.75pp), JNJ (+0.70pp), AAPL (+0.56pp), LLY (+0.44pp), XOM (+0.33pp), PLD (+0.29pp), GE/CVX (+0.21-0.24pp) show positive excess drift vs SPY, and none of these edges is statistically distinguishable from zero at a 5-day horizon. Limitations: (1) drift over 5 days is dominated by noise; momentum/mean-reversion signals (e.g., XOM RSI 83.9, CVX RSI 92 overbought; GOOGL/CAT/SHW/LIN oversold RSI ~26-31) are not explicitly modeled and could flip short-horizon direction; (2) intervals assume approximately lognormal returns with recent-vol scaling and do not capture fat tails, jumps, earnings gaps, or vol clustering; (3) no news, fundamentals, or post-decision-date information is used; (4) correlations across tickers are ignored, so portfolio-level uncertainty is narrower than the sum of individual intervals suggests; (5) TLT/GLD interval widths reflect low/high vol regimes respectively and may shift if rates or dollar regimes change abruptly.

research.summary: The week was dominated by Big Tech Q2 earnings dispersion: Microsoft (+15% on Azure guidance) and Amazon (+15% on best revenue growth in four years) rallied, while Apple tumbled 7.4% on the decision date itself after a fiscal Q3 miss, downgrade, and AI-driven component shortages, and Meta fell ~9% despite 28% revenue growth as investors balked at AI cash burn. The July 29 FOMC statement was followed by coverage describing a hawkish, higher-for-longer stance (mortgage rates at 6.66%), pressuring duration (TLT -3.8% 30d) while the Iran war supply squeeze drove record energy profits (CVX beat with largest-ever quarterly profit; XOM missed despite $14.7B). forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call (drift method) for all 26 tickers over the brief's 5-trading-day horizon (2026-07-31 to 2026-08-07), using only data through the decision date. Benchmark SPY expected +0.35% (p10 -1.93%, p90 +2.69%); all expected returns should be judged against that, not zero. Highest expected excess returns vs SPY: CAT +1.00%, GOOGL +0.87%, JNJ +0.56%, LLY +0.46%, AAPL +0.38%, XOM +0.42%; notable laggards: META -0.82%, AMT -0.79%, MSFT -0.51%. Confidence is a signal-to-noise heuristic (|expected return| relative to the p10-p90 interval width), so it stays near 0.5 everywhere: at a 5-day horizon, expected drift is small relative to per-name volatility and no forecast is high-conviction. Limitations: the drift model uses no news, fundamentals, or mean-reversion/oversold dynamics, so it does not price RSI extremes (MSFT 75, XOM 74.4, CVX 74.6 overbought; META 23.4, CAT 28.2, LIN 23.7 oversold) or momentum-crash risk in high-vol names (CAT 51.8% vol, META 53.2%, MSFT 55.3%, AMZN 55.1%); 12-1 momentum signals have weak predictive power over 5 days; intervals are symmetric and assume roughly lognormal returns, underweighting fat tails and gap risk; TLT/GLD/SPY intervals are narrow due to low realized vol but regime shifts (rates, risk-off) are not modeled.

forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call (one-shot budget) produced drift-based 5-trading-day return forecasts for all 25 tradable tickers plus the SPY benchmark, using only price history through the 2026-08-07 decision date. p10/p90 are the tool's 10th/90th percentile bounds; confidence is the implied one-sided probability that the sign of the return matches the direction, derived from expected return scaled by the interval width ((p90-p10)/2.563 as a 5-day sigma proxy). Benchmark comparison: SPY is forecast at +0.40% (p10 -1.92%, p90 +2.77%), so only GOOGL (+0.79% excess), CAT (+0.91%), JNJ (+0.51%), AAPL (+0.35%), LLY (+0.36%), XOM (+0.28%), GE (+0.22%), PLD (+0.18%) and GLD (+0.11%) clear the benchmark on expected return, and all by margins far smaller than their interval widths - these are weak edges, not high-conviction signals. Limitations: (1) the drift method extrapolates recent trend and ignores mean reversion, valuation, fundamentals, earnings dates and news; (2) at a 5-day horizon expected returns are near zero and dominated by volatility, so wide intervals reflect genuine uncertainty rather than avoidability - e.g., CAT's +1.31% mean sits inside a -5.5%/+8.7% band and its 30d momentum crash (-10.09%, 47.9% vol) argues the drift estimate may be optimistic; (3) intervals assume approximately normal, i.i.d. returns and understate fat tails and vol clustering (MSFT RSI 81.1 after +30% in 30d, META/CAT ~50%+ vol are candidates for wider realized dispersion); (4) no cross-asset correlation structure is modeled, so portfolio-level risk cannot be inferred from these marginals alone.

Expected returns are small relative to interval widths: only CAT (+1.34%, +0.92% excess), GOOGL (+1.12%, +0.70%), JNJ (+0.86%, +0.44%), LLY (+0.85%, +0.43%), XOM (+0.84%, +0.42%), and AAPL (+0.80%, +0.38%) clear the benchmark by a meaningful margin, while META (-0.52%, -0.94% excess) and AMT (-0.30%, -0.72%) lag it. Confidence scores reflect excess-vs-benchmark magnitude relative to interval width, not absolute return. Limitations: (1) drift estimates over 5 days are dominated by noise; p10-p90 spans of 3-14 points mean most directions are statistically indistinguishable from the benchmark; (2) intervals are Gaussian scalings of 30-day annualized vol and understate fat tails and jump risk; (3) no news, fundamentals, or mean-reversion signals are incorporated - notably MSFT (RSI 86.3, +23.5% 30d) and AAPL (RSI 27.0, -8.1% 30d) sit at RSI extremes where drift assumptions are weakest; (4) CAT's top excess return conflicts with its -19.4% drawdown and 38% vol, so its point estimate carries crash risk the interval only partially captures; (5) forecasts are price-only and exclude dividends and transaction costs (10 bps each way), which are material relative to 5-day expected returns.

forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call for all 26 tickers (25 tradable + SPY benchmark) over the brief's 5-trading-day horizon (2026-08-21 to 2026-08-28), using only data through the decision date. Method is statistical drift: expected return is the p50 of a distribution centered on recent drift, with p10/p90 from 30-day annualized volatility scaled to 5 days. Benchmark comparison: SPY is forecast at +0.38% (p10 -1.91%, p90 +2.72%), so only names with expected returns above ~0.4% (CAT +1.39%, LLY +1.34%, GOOGL +1.05%, XOM +0.94%, JNJ +0.90%, CVX +0.66%, PLD +0.66%, GLD +0.61%, AAPL +0.60%) show positive expected excess return; META is the only name forecast below benchmark with a down direction. Confidence is scaled by expected return relative to interval width and is uniformly modest (0.50-0.56) because at a 5-day horizon the p10-p90 bands (roughly +/-3% to +/-7% for equities) are an order of magnitude wider than expected returns - wide intervals reflect uncertainty, not avoidance, but they also mean no single-name edge is statistically decisive. Limitations: drift/vol model only - no news, fundamentals, or cross-asset correlation structure; assumes return distribution is roughly symmetric and volatility is stable over the horizon; short-horizon drift estimates have low signal-to-noise; GLD's RSI 82.5 and LLY/JNJ/XOM/CVX RSI >70 suggest overbought conditions the model does not capture; direction labels 'flat' denote |expected| < ~0.5% where the sign is not meaningful.

Instead I stay invested in confirmed multi-horizon leaders, trimming laggard AAPL (worst 30d relative performer, sitting on SMA50 with unverified CEO-transition noise) from 6.5% to 4% and redeploying into the highest-quality non-overbought trends V (52w high, 19% vol), JPM (uptrend consolidation) and SHW (+11.9% 30d/+12.6% 90d at RSI 46), while holding LLY/JNJ/XOM/CVX per multi-horizon strength discipline rather than selling winners solely on RSI>70. NVDA stays at just 3% through Wednesday's earnings (a ±8% gap moves the portfolio only ~±0.24% and the book has no other AI-complex exposure), with ~18% cash retained as the deliberate event-week buffer given the 39% overbought cluster and TLT's dead hedge; turnover of ~7% costs under 1bp.

forecaster.method_notes: Drift-based statistical forecast over the 5-trading-day horizon (2026-08-28 to 2026-09-04) using only data through the decision date; one forecast_universe call supplied all tickers including benchmark SPY. Expected returns are small relative to interval widths: at a 5-day horizon, per-ticker volatility (e.g., SPY ~1.9% p10-p90 half-width vs +0.37% expected; NVDA ~5.3% vs +0.35%) dominates the drift signal, so most tickers are statistically indistinguishable from the benchmark's +0.37% expected return. Confidence values are implied probabilities of the stated direction given a normal approximation with sigma=(p90-p10)/2.563. Relative to SPY, the strongest expected excess returns are CAT (+0.93pp, but widest interval and momentum-crash profile per snapshot), GOOGL (+0.67pp), LLY (+0.65pp), JNJ (+0.50pp, tightest high-conviction interval), and XOM (+0.43pp); the weakest are META (-0.91pp), HD (-0.66pp), and AMT (-0.57pp). Wide p10-p90 intervals represent uncertainty, not a recommendation to avoid; only META has a negative expected return with meaningful downside skew. Limitations: the drift model ignores news, earnings, mean reversion, and regime shifts; volatility is estimated from a 30-day window and may understate event risk; short-horizon expected returns have low signal-to-noise and should not be over-trusted for sizing; no knowledge of anything after 2026-08-28 is used.

Turnover is ~10% one-way (~1bp cost) against ~6bps of avoided cash drag, and I hold rather than trim the overbought V/CVX since their trends and relative strength remain intact.

forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call as of 2026-09-04 for the 4-trading-day horizon (decision 2026-09-04 to next decision 2026-09-11). Method: drift-based statistical model using only price history through the decision date; expected returns are small drift estimates while p10/p90 intervals are scaled from each ticker's 30-day annualized volatility, so interval width dominates the point estimate at this short horizon. Benchmark comparison: SPY expected +0.30% over the same window; only CAT (+0.70pp), LLY (+0.49pp), GOOGL (+0.46pp), JNJ (+0.42pp), AAPL (+0.24pp) and XOM (+0.30pp) show positive expected excess vs SPY, and all excesses are well inside the noise band of the intervals — treat direction calls as weak signals, not high-conviction. Limitations: no news, fundamentals, or post-decision-date information is used; volatility is assumed stationary over the window (no vol clustering or fat tails); drift estimates over 4 days are statistically noisy; correlations between tickers are not modeled; TLT/GLD/REIT intervals reflect their own vols and may understate regime-shift risk (e.g., rate moves).

Holding ~16% cash is justified by observed risks, not missing news: the September FOMC falls inside the window with a genuinely split rate path, SPY breadth has deteriorated (12/25 below SMA50) at stalled momentum, and the marginal redeployment targets would only concentrate already-large energy/financials positions for ~1-2bps of extra expected excess; total round-trip cost of the rebalance is ~4bps, negligible against the risk removed.

forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call as of 2026-09-11 for the 5-trading-day horizon (next decision 2026-09-18). Method is a drift-based statistical model: expected return is a small positive drift estimated from recent price history only, with p10/p90 bands from 30-day annualized volatility scaled to 5 trading days (approximately normal assumption). Benchmark SPY is forecast at +0.35% (p10 -1.93%, p90 +2.68%); all excess returns are measured against that, not zero. Key readings: strongest expected excess returns are CAT +0.97%, GOOGL +0.56%, LLY/JNJ +0.48%, XOM +0.43%; weakest are HD -0.82%, META -0.60%, SHW -0.57%, AMT -0.54%. Limitations: (1) expected returns over 5 days are tiny relative to the p10-p90 widths (e.g., NVDA -6.17% to +7.51%), so direction labels are weak signals and intervals are uncertainty, not avoidance verdicts; (2) the model ignores news, fundamentals, earnings, and regime shifts, and assumes constant volatility with no fat tails, vol clustering, or mean reversion; (3) META's RSI 84.4 and LLY's RSI 2.6 indicate recent moves the drift model does not explicitly correct for; (4) SPY is comparison-only and not tradable in the universe. Confidence values reflect interval width relative to expected excess return, not probability of positive return.

forecaster.method_notes: Drift-based statistical forecast over the 5-trading-day horizon (2026-09-18 to 2026-09-25), using only data through the decision date. Expected returns are annualized drift scaled to the horizon; p10/p90 are normal quantiles from 30-day annualized volatility scaled to 5 days. Benchmark SPY is forecast at +0.34% (p10 -1.95%, p90 +2.67%), so only names with expected returns above ~+0.34% (CAT +1.28, LLY +0.88, JNJ +0.85, XOM +0.83, GOOGL +0.78, AAPL +0.68, CVX +0.67, NVDA +0.54) clear the benchmark on expectation; most tickers are statistically indistinguishable from SPY over this short window. Confidence reflects the probability the sign of the realized return matches the direction given the forecast distribution (flat = ~0.5, i.e., no sign edge). forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call (drift method) for all 26 tickers over the brief's 5-trading-day horizon (2026-09-25 to 2026-10-02), using only data through the decision date. Expected returns are drift estimates; p10/p90 are 10th/90th percentile return intervals scaled from each ticker's 30d annualized vol. Benchmark comparison: SPY expected +0.32% over 5 days, so only AAPL (+0.71), LLY (+0.90), JNJ (+0.87), XOM (+0.75), CVX (+0.58), GOOGL (+0.61) and CAT (+1.25) show positive expected excess; HD (-0.65) is the only clear negative. All expected returns are small relative to interval widths (e.g., NVDA +/-6-7pp), so directional calls carry low conviction and wide intervals reflect genuine 5-day uncertainty, not avoidance signals. Limitations: drift at a 5-day horizon is dominated by noise; no news, fundamentals, or event risk (e.g., LLY's Sept 30 readout) is incorporated; Gaussian intervals understate fat tails; extreme RSI readings (AAPL 74.6, META 77.8, NEE 16.4, SO 19.5) imply mean-reversion risk not captured by the drift model; CAT's high expected return coexists with a confirmed momentum-crash profile (90d -17.5%, -22.7% off high), so its +1.25% point estimate should be treated cautiously.
